podcast.title: Citizen Dick Fictional Band Role
podcast.body: Actor Matt Dillon was to be part of a fictional band in the movie *Singles*, along with Jeff Ament, Eddie Vedder, and Stone Gossard. Jeff Ament was tasked with creating names for this group, and "Citizen Dick" was the chosen name from his list of options. "Jeff Amit had been given the task of coming up with a name for a fictional band that he, Eddie and Stone and Matt Dillon, one of the stars of the film, would be in, so he listed a bunch of options."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Singles (1992) – Walk-On Cameo and Spoonman Song Origin
xref.body: Director Cameron Crowe cast Cornell in a brief, non-speaking walk-on role in *Singles* (1991, released 1992), appearing after a scene where Matt Dillon shows Bridget Fonda his new car stereo, immediately preceding a Soundgarden concert sequence. "Chris Cornell walks up to see what's going on. It doesn't say anything, but the very next shot is of Chris and Soundgarden on stage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Singles Cameo (1992) – Eddie, Stone, and Jeff as Citizen Dick Members
xref.body: In Cameron Crowe's Seattle-set film *Singles* (filmed 1991, released 1992), Eddie Vedder, Stone Gossard, and Jeff Ament appear as the backing band for fictional singer Cliff Poncier (played by Matt Dillon), in a band called Citizen Dick. Their longest appearance is just over a minute, showing them reading a review of their record. By the time the film was released, Pearl Jam was enormous, which worked greatly in the film's favor. Pearl Jam also contributed two songs to the soundtrack: "Breath" and "State of Love and Trust." "By the time the movie was released in 1992, the band was huge."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
